subject.title: [Feature]: Feature request: Per-agent isolated browser instances with per-profile proxy support (concurrent execution)

question: Should OpenClaw add per-profile managed-browser proxy config plus per-agent/subagent default browser-profile binding, and what security model should govern proxy credentials, SSRF enforcement, and profile selection?
rationale: The requested feature adds public config/API surface and changes browser egress plus cookie/session isolation semantics; automation cannot choose that security boundary safely from source inspection alone.

options.title: Approve a gated browser-profile design
options.body: Add the feature only with a documented contract for secret-safe proxy auth, explicit SSRF proxy trust, profile inheritance/override rules, resource limits, and upgrade-safe config validation.

options.title: Keep explicit profile and global proxy workarounds
options.body: Decline first-class per-agent/per-profile config for now and document current explicit profile, browser.extraArgs, remote CDP, and node-host patterns as the supported path.

options.title: Split into canonical narrower issues
options.body: Move proxy egress to the broader proxy issue and browser ownership/inheritance to the subagent session issue, then close this umbrella after both paths are linked.

recommendation.title: Approve a gated browser-profile design
recommendation.body: Add the feature only with a documented contract for secret-safe proxy auth, explicit SSRF proxy trust, profile inheritance/override rules, resource limits, and upgrade-safe config validation.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent browser plugin and docs ownership makes this the best available routing target for the product/security decision.
